reviews.summary: 对 NocoBase3 基础框架在 Issue #651（项目协作：任务与成果验收）上的独立评审。选取 6 个能力单位：数据建模与迁移、HTTP API 与错误契约、成员可见性与授权、后台作业与通知提醒、文件存储与内容访问、客户端路由装配。5 个维度的框架评分均落在 76–92 分区间：框架原语（defineMigration/defineSeed、defineApiRoutes/ApiError、authorization composite、ScheduleExecutor+notification、file repository manager、app-client 路由）均完整且多数有贴近用例的指引示例。本轮 verify-3 的三处失败经源码对照归因为 Agent/业务实现缺陷（分享字段名不一致、根内容路由未映射领域错误导致不透明 500、任务行编辑表单未预填），而非框架缺陷；框架侧仅记录一条文档改进建议（根路由缺少应用级 onError 兜底的提示不够直白），以及一条“指引与需求匹配度高”的优点。verify-4 已通过 C01。

findings.title: 根内容路由未映射领域错误，成员预览/下载成果返回不透明 500
findings.detail: 成员访问未被分享的成果内容路径时，deliverable-files.ts 的根路由直接抛 ProjectCollaborationError。该错误的 status 为字符串（如 INVALID_ARGUMENT），apiErrorHandler 的 recognizeApiError 只接受数字 400–499，于是 rethrow；根路由又没有应用级 onError 兜底，最终由 Hono 返回 text/plain 500。负责人会话同一接口返回 200，说明是实现层错误映射缺失，而非能力缺失。repair-3 在根路由补上 toApiError 映射后恢复。
findings.impact: 成员无法预览或下载成果文件，验收项直接判失败（verify-3 C01 failed）。

findings.title: 指引未点明根路由没有应用级 onError 兜底
findings.detail: application/index.js 在 line 260 对 /api 设置 api.onError，随后在 line 303 通过 this.router.route('/', router) 挂载根贡献，根路由没有对应的应用级错误翻译。server-routes.md 说明根路由“不受 /api 规则约束”，但没有明确提醒：一旦根路由抛出未映射的领域错误，就会得到不透明 500。这使 F1 这类失误在缺乏兜底时更难定位。
findings.impact: 开发者按文档实现根路由时容易遗漏错误映射，错误表现为不透明 500，排障成本高。
findings.suggestedChange: 在 server-routes.md 增加一句：根路由不会继承 /api 的 api.onError 行为，需自带 onError 或将领域错误映射为 ApiError。

diagnosis.trigger: 应用在根路径注册贡献并抛出未映射的领域错误
diagnosis.expected: 指引明确提醒根路由需自行挂 onError 或统一映射领域错误
diagnosis.actual: 指引只说根路由不受 /api 规则约束，未点出缺少应用级兜底会产生不透明 500
diagnosis.workaround: 每个根路由自行挂 onError 并映射领域错误
diagnosis.acceptance: server-routes.md 增补根路由错误翻译说明，并有端到端用例覆盖根路由错误码

feedbackReview.reason: F2 是 guidance-gap：冻结的 server-routes.md 只说明根路由不在 /api 下、响应按第三方协议而非标准 /api body 组织，全文没有 onError/apiErrorHandler 或“根路由需自带错误翻译”的提醒；application/index.js 只在为 /api 新建的 router 上安装 api.onError，根贡献经 this.router.route('/', router) 单独挂载且外层 router 无错误翻译，因此根路由抛出未被 recognizeApiError 识别的领域错误时得到不透明 500。E73 的应用根内容路由正因此自行 mapDomainError+onError，E80 记录过同类成员访问返回 500 的现象。建议只是补一句提醒，未把愿望当违约，也未要求新框架能力；环境与工厂因素均不能解释该缺口。六项检查均有原始证据。

checks.reason: server-routes.md（E49, 179-201）对根路由的承诺是：根路由不在 /api 下，响应取决于第三方协议而非标准 /api body，也不进 API 文档；同一文件仅在 /api 语境中说“按 http-api.md 组织响应与错误”（行14），全文无 onError/apiErrorHandler。E48（http-api.md, 135-141）把错误兜底描述为“应用会处理路由没处理的一切”并给出 apiErrorHandler，但该契约按 /api 编写，未点明根路由不继承它。故原结论“指引只讲不受 /api 约束、未点出缺少应用级兜底”与冻结文档一致。

E47（application/index.js, 245-303）显示 api.onError(...) 只装在为 /api 新建的 Hono 上，随后 this.router.route('/api', api)；根贡献另行 this.router.route('/', router) 挂载，外层 router 未注册 onError；defineRootRoutes 也只设置 scope:'root'。E73（deliverable-files.ts, 36-64）的应用根内容路由因此自带 router.onError(mapDomainError)+apiErrorHandler，注释直述不翻译会把权限拒绝变成不透明 500。实现行为支持“根路由没有应用级错误兜底”。

F2 是对文档的改进项，不主张应用违约；E73 显示应用已用正确方式在根路由自行挂 onError 并映射领域错误，说明该前提在实践中必须被显式满足。E80 记录 verify-3 中成员预览/下载 /deliverables/.../content 返回 HTTP 500 text/plain、而负责人同接口返回 200，正是根路由缺少映射/兜底时的表现（后由 F1 修复）。未见应用误用 API 的反证。
现象完全由进程内 Hono 路由装配决定：E47 展示 onError 的安装点与根贡献的挂载位置，不需要外部服务、凭据、依赖安装或特殊运行环境即可解释；没有环境材料显示另有原因。环境既不能解释该指引缺口，也不构成反证。
F2 指向随应用冻结的 app/.agents/skills/nocobase-app-development/references/server-routes.md（E49），属于随产品交付的应用开发指引，不是工厂提示、注入配置或 QA/构建脚本的产物；没有工厂材料显示模板覆盖或注入造成该表述，故保留为文档自身的表述缺口。

已有文档确实提供通用错误能力：E48 说明 apiErrorHandler 是唯一错误 API、路由自身的 onError 先运行；E46 说明它识别已知错误并 rethrow 其余、应用最终给出不透明 500。但两者都按 /api 语境书写，未指出根路由不继承 api 路由的 onError；server-routes.md 也只在行14 泛化地指向 http-api.md。现有入口能实现映射能力，却不能替代这句根路由专属提醒，改进空间成立。

processNotes.author: implementer
processNotes.summary: Repaired the four failures browser QA observed. The share dialog sent `sharedWithId` while the API requires `userId`, so sharing always failed. The deliverable content root route let an unmapped `ProjectCollaborationError` through `apiErrorHandler`, turning a member's permission denial into an opaque 500. The reused `TaskDialog` never reapplied `defaultValues`, so a row's Edit form opened empty. The overdue-task reminder job sent to a channel the application had not configured and had no production inbox surface at all. Added the notification channel, a `/notifications` App route, targeted component/API tests, and updated client/server AGENTS.md.

blockers.title: createAppTest application refuses to start without AUTH_SECRET, and cookie-authenticated writes are then refused without a trusted Origin
blockers.symptom: Starting the app-test application failed with ApplicationNotConfiguredError: auth.secret is not set. After supplying a secret, every signed-in POST/DELETE answered 403 INVALID_CSRF_ORIGIN while the equivalent GET succeeded.
blockers.rootCause: A test run has no config.yml and no dotenv files, so auth.secret and app.publicOrigin are empty. signIn() from the authentication testing helper addresses http://localhost but builds its Request without an Origin header, and the authentication provider rejects any cookie-bearing write whose origin is not trusted.
blockers.resolution: Set process.env.AUTH_SECRET at the top of the test file, pass server: { env: { APP_PUBLIC_ORIGIN: 'http://localhost' } } to createAppTest, and wrap each signed-in session so its fetch always sets Origin: http://localhost. Documented in server/AGENTS.md.
blockers.cost: Three test iterations (startup failure, then two rounds of 403s) before the pattern was clear.

blockers.title: eslint --max-warnings 0 rejected unnecessary assertions and an unbound destructured method
blockers.symptom: pnpm lint failed with 8 errors: 5 @typescript-eslint/no-unnecessary-type-assertion in server/providers/projects.ts (values/Partial<ProjectRow> and Partial<MilestoneRow> casts), 1 in server/routes/deliverable-files.ts (parseBody cast), 1 unbound-method on the destructured repository from the seed run context, and 1 prefer-const on the seed's memberId.
blockers.rootCause: Defensive `as Partial<...>` casts were left on values the Repository create/update receivers already accept, the seed destructured the SeedContext.repository method (declared as a method, not a function property) and then called it free-standing, and memberId was declared with let though never reassigned.
blockers.resolution: Removed the redundant casts, changed `run({ query, repository })` to take the context and call context.repository(...), and changed memberId to const. Re-ran eslint on the three files (clean) and tsc -p tsconfig.server.json --noEmit (clean); prettier reports the files already formatted.

blockers.title: Baseline route test pins the page authorization of every signed-in page, so the new project pages failed it
blockers.symptom: tests/logic/client-routes.test.ts > 'pins the page authorization of every signed-in page' failed: expected [ { name: 'home', authorizedAs: null } ] but received the five app signed-in pages (home, projects, projects.new, project-detail, project-task), each with authorizedAs null.
blockers.rootCause: The application added four App routes with auth: 'required' (projects, projects.new, project-detail, project-task), all with authz: 'skip' because project access is membership checked server-side. The test intentionally lists every signed-in App page in depth-first order; it is designed to be extended when a new signed-in page is added, and the new pages were never added to its list.
blockers.resolution: Added the four new signed-in pages to the pinned list in tests/logic/client-routes.test.ts, each resolving to authorizedAs null because their authz is 'skip'. Verified with `pnpm exec vitest run tests/logic/client-routes.test.ts` (3 passed) plus prettier and eslint on the file.

blockers.title: The Share dialog always failed: the client posted `sharedWithId` while the API requires `userId`
blockers.symptom: QA selected a member in the share dialog and clicked Share; POST /api/deliverables/{id}/shares answered 400 INVALID_INPUT with field `userId` ("expected string, received undefined"), the dialog kept showing "It is not shared with anyone yet.", so sharing and revoking were both unverifiable.
blockers.rootCause: client/pages/projects/deliverables.tsx sent `{ sharedWithId: pendingId }`, but ShareDeliverableInput and the route take `{ userId }`. The server-side API test already posted `userId`, so only the browser path was wrong and the test suite could not see it.
blockers.resolution: Send `{ userId: pendingId }` from the Share dialog. The existing API test already covers the server contract, and the new content test exercises share → allow and revoke through the same `userId` field.

blockers.title: Deliverable content returned 500 for a member without a share because the root route never mapped the domain error
blockers.symptom: A member's Preview/Download fetched /deliverables/{id}/content and got HTTP 500 text/plain "Internal Server Error" inside the iframe, while the owner got 200 application/pdf.
blockers.rootCause: The content endpoint is a `defineRootRoutes` route, so it has its own `onError`. It called `apiErrorHandler(error, context)` directly; `apiErrorHandler` rethrows errors it does not recognize, and `ProjectCollaborationError` thrown by `assertDeliverableContentAccess` is only converted to an `ApiError` by the private `toApiError` helper in routes/collaboration.ts. A permission denial therefore surfaced as an opaque 500.
blockers.resolution: Exported `toApiError` from routes/collaboration.ts and ran the content and upload routers' errors through a `mapDomainError` that converts a `ProjectCollaborationError` before `apiErrorHandler`. Added an API test that uploads a file, submits an owner deliverable, asserts the member gets 403 DELIVERABLE_CONTENT_DENIED (not 500), then shares and asserts the member gets the 200 bytes.

blockers.title: A reused Edit-task dialog opened empty because react-hook-form defaultValues only apply at mount
blockers.symptom: The task row's "Edit task" dialog showed empty Title/Description, Assignee=Unassigned, Milestone=No milestone, Priority=Normal instead of the task's values; the detail drawer's Edit task prefilled correctly.
blockers.rootCause: TaskDialog is mounted once by the list and re-rendered with a different `task` prop, but `useForm({ defaultValues: taskValues })` captures values only on first mount. The drawer mounts with the task already present, which is why it worked. Changing `task` never repopulated the form.
blockers.resolution: Extracted `taskFormValues(task)` and added `useEffect(() => { if (open) form.reset(taskFormValues(task)); }, [open, task, form])`, so opening the dialog resets to the task being edited (or clears for create). Added tests/components/task-dialog-prefill.test.tsx, which re-renders the dialog for a second task and asserts the Title/Description/Deadline inputs follow it.

blockers.title: The overdue reminder was dropped: no configured notification channel and no production inbox surface
blockers.symptom: QA found no notification bell or center, and Settings → Automation showed no workflows or scheduled tasks; the daily overdue reminder could not be observed at all.
blockers.rootCause: providers/project-reminders.ts sent `messages: { 'in-app': ... }`, but server/config/notification.ts declared `notification.channels: {}`, so the send failed on an unknown Channel and the error was swallowed by the per-task catch. Separately, the notification-in-app client plugin only contributes a development-only inbox page (`/dev/notification-in-app`), so a production build had no inbox a user could open, and an immediate reminder at startup was not possible because the schedule was cron-only.
blockers.resolution: Configured `notification.channels.inbox: { provider: 'in-app' }`, switched the reminder to the `inbox` channel, and set the schedule's `immediately: true` so the first firing (job creation) reminds the overdue work already present; the `overdue-task:<taskId>:<date>` idempotency key keeps later restarts from repeating it. Added the App route /notifications (client/pages/notifications.tsx) wrapping the plugin's NotificationInAppProvider/Inbox as the production surface, with navigation.notifications in both locales. Added an API test that waits for the assignee's /api/notificationInApp/messages to contain the overdue reminder.

improvements.title: @nocobase/date-picker cannot be used offline because date-fns and react-day-picker are not linked
improvements.detail: The UI guidance points at @nocobase/date-picker, but adding it only works if date-fns and react-day-picker resolve at the application root, and the default template has them in the pnpm store only. Rather than add and link dependencies mid-feature, the due-date fields use a native <input type="date">, which is a deviation from the guidance.
improvements.suggestedChange: Link date-fns and react-day-picker at the application root (or make the @nocobase/date-picker item self-contained) so an application can add the recommended date field without a dependency change.

improvements.title: App tests must discover the trusted origin and session secret themselves
improvements.detail: signIn() and createAppTest work for reads without extra setup, but the first cookie-authenticated write fails on CSRF unless the test pins APP_PUBLIC_ORIGIN and sets an Origin header, and nothing in testing.md or the helper signatures says so.
improvements.suggestedChange: Have createAppTest/signIn default to a trusted origin and a generated AUTH_SECRET, or state the two required settings in references/testing.md.

improvements.title: A root route needs the same domain-error mapping as the /api router that owns the same service
improvements.detail: collaboration.ts mapped ProjectCollaborationError to ApiError privately. deliverable-files.ts reuses the same service from a defineRootRoutes router, so an unhandled domain error there reverted to an opaque 500 for exactly the permission path the endpoint exists to enforce. The framework's apiErrorHandler intentionally rethrows unrecognized errors, but nothing points a second router at the mapping its sibling already has.
improvements.suggestedChange: Document (or provide) a shared domain-error mapping so every router backed by one service maps the service's error type, rather than each route author rediscovering apiErrorHandler's rethrow behavior.

Boundaries that are easy to get wrong:

- `findOne` takes the first match; `updateOne` and `deleteOne` require exactly one; `upsertOne` requires a unique equality condition.
- `updateMany` and `deleteMany` refuse an empty scope. Pass `all: true` only when the task explicitly calls for every row — never to make an error go away.
- `createMany` and `updateMany` do not accept nested relation writes. `createOne` accepts `create` and `connect` on a relation, not the full set.
- `disconnect` detaches; `delete` removes the target record. A relation target update or delete stays inside the current parent record's scope.
- Repository does not apply the application's permissions. A route handler decides what the caller may see and change _before_ anything reaches `filter`, `values` or `select`. `writePolicy` defaults to `true` for an internal Repository and `false` for one reached from an API route, so a route-facing Repository needs an explicit allow list.

The application handles everything a route does not:

- An unexpected error becomes `500 INTERNAL` with reason `INTERNAL_ERROR` and nothing about its cause; the stack goes to the request log.
- Hono's `HTTPException`, and an error carrying a 4xx `status` such as `AuthorizationDeniedError`, keep their status.

One the caller can act on keeps its code as `reason` with domain `app`, its `path` and `details` in `metadata`, and, when the input is invalid, its path as a field violation: a refused write is `403`, a missing record `404`, a version conflict `409`, invalid input or a missing relation target the body names `400`. ## Implement in this order

1. Declare schema and relationships through self-contained migrations. Choose stable composite, page and data scope names. Keep authorization decisions out of migration code.
2. Declare reusable collection permissions with `defineDatabasePermission`; compose user-facing business operations as composite resources with `defineCompositeResource` from `@nocobase/authorization/core`. Explicitly name fields, relation capabilities and every collection a workflow touches.
3. In the owning provider's `boot`, opt collections in with `authz.database.collections.add`, register composites with `authz.compositeResources.define`, record access with `authz.recordAccess.define` and settings items with `authz.settings.add`. Then add a workspace subsection with `authz.ui.sections.add({ name, title, parent })` and list each composite or settings item in it with `authz.ui.place(reference, { section, group? })` (the permission workspace lists sections and subsections on the left and the selected subsection's resources, under optional `authz.ui.groups`, on the right; an unplaced composite or settings item goes under its default section's Other with a startup warning, and a misplaced one fails a development start). Pages are not registered on the server: the client route tree lists them. Release subject registrations at shutdown.
4. Protect every server route with authentication. For a simple single-scope Repository operation, keep `defineRepositoryApiRoutes` and add `authz.database.authorizeRepository` to map methods to composite actions; it reuses or initializes the request's authorization context. For workflows, persisted-state checks, multiple data scopes or custom responses, install `authz.middleware()`, call `c.get('authz').authorize()` once and bind every returned collection policy with `repository.withPolicy()`. Follow [Repository route integration](references/repository-routes.md).
5. Declare `authz` on every entry client route (nested pages inherit it; an omitted one defaults to root-only or `'skip'` with a development warning), add `useCan` for action visibility and obtain per-record eligibility from the server when needed. Handle pending and error states without displaying stale access.
6. Complete the accompanying permission configuration from the responsibility matrix: sets, page and action grants, selected data scopes, supported rules and intended assignments. Use seeds for fresh installations and authorized provisioning for existing installations; editing a seed does not update a running App. Resolve optional capabilities through their installed Skills and preserve unrelated administrator edits.
7. Verify denied as well as allowed requests through the production route factory and actual database policies. Then verify the UI with ordinary users and inherited memberships.

## Enforcement rules

- Register collections explicitly with `authz.database.collections.add({ name, title, actions? })`. Metadata comes from the database; registration grants nothing. Unregistered collections are denied even to unrestricted users.
- `settings`, `composite` and `database.collection` are catalog types: a check on an unregistered item or action is denied with `RESOURCE_ACTION_NOT_SUPPORTED`. `page`, `user`, `notification` and Hub types are record types that declare actions only; their grants use `id: '*'` for every record.
- A composite action composes exactly the grants it lists, never another composite. A data scope targets the one collection its grant actions name, whose type must declare `recordAccess` (`database.collection` does). Grant page access separately; a page grant never authorizes a server endpoint.
- `can` is for feature visibility. `require` needs an unconditional permit and rejects conditional decisions. Business endpoints use `authorize`, reject denial or missing policies, and consume `conditions.database` without resolving collection grants again.
- For simple business CRUD, keep the Repository route definition and bind each method to its composite action with `authz.database.authorizeRepository`. Multi-scope actions and workflow transitions need custom handlers. `authz.database.policyFor` folds collection grants; without its third argument it does not respect a business-action boundary.
- Scope every read and write in the workflow, including parent lookups. Keep multi-record writes transactional and include expected business state in mutation predicates. Authorization does not validate a quote's amount or its workflow transition.
- Fields and relation operations are code-owned. The permission workspace configures pages, business actions, their data scopes and settings items; do not build a second raw-field permission editor.
- Relation writes do not inherit the target collection's standalone constraints. Declare target record access and join-table fields explicitly; keep foreign-key fields from bypassing association controls.
- An authorization context caches grants and rules. Reuse one within a request; create a new one for a new request or identity. Do not persist decisions in module state.

`name` is the Client resource; `collection` defaults to name, `connection` to the database default, and `accessPath` to `/uploads/<name>`. Disk is required. Content paths contain static alphanumeric, underscore or hyphen segments, start with `/`, and have no trailing slash.

Only declared POST `/api/<name>/<action>` operations are exposed; `name` is a camelCase path segment such as `invoiceAttachments`. Ordinary actions are `findMany/findOne/count/exists/aggregate/groupBy/createOne/updateOne/deleteOne`. There are no createMany/updateMany/deleteMany HTTP actions.

Every exposed action appears in the application's API document at `/api/swagger/docs` (JSON at `/api/swagger`), under the exposure's name as its tag with operationIds such as `invoiceAttachmentsFindMany` and `invoiceAttachmentsUploadOne`. The upload operations are documented as `multipart/form-data` with their `maxSize`, `201` result and `400`/`403`/`413`/`415` errors; read it there rather than guessing a request shape. The content route under `accessPath` is outside `/api` and is not in the document.

`policy` is required and governs every action of the exposure, uploads included. It is a Repository Policy: `read`, `create`, `update` and `delete`, each `true`, `false`, or a rule node. A node that is `false` refuses that operation; a node with no `fields` accepts no caller-supplied field, which is what a metadata `createOne` needs before it will accept anything. Pass a function of the principal — `policy: (principal) => ({ ... })` — together with a `principal(context)` resolver to scope rows to the caller; without a principal the request is refused with 403.

An upload supplies no caller fields, so it binds a Policy derived from this one: the `create` scope and defaults are inherited and the field allowlist is replaced by the file columns. `create: false` therefore forbids uploading as well as creating metadata — decided, with the principal, before the body limit, the content type or the multipart body is read, so a refused upload answers `403 WRITE_FORBIDDEN` (domain `app`) and stores nothing — and a `create.defaults` of `{ ownerId }` is stamped onto uploaded rows — which is what keeps an uploaded file inside the same scope `findMany` reads. The content route under `accessPath` is the exception: it is public and this Policy does not reach it.

Content is GET `<accessPath>/<uuid>.<ext>` outside `/api`, omitting the dot when extensionless. Stream returns full bytes as an attachment; redirect returns a public storage URL or a five-minute signed URL. A disk without URL support requires stream mode; there is no automatic fallback.

These are public routes. For restricted files, register App-owned authentication and authorization on the paths each contribution owns before mounting it — `/<name>/<action>` per exposed API action, `<accessPath>/*` for content. Never `router.use('*', ...)` in a contribution router: contributions share the mounted router, so it also guards the SPA and every contribution mounted after yours. Check the operation and record/parent-record access; a login page, private disk, Client filter or Policy field allowlist is not authentication. Add scoped middleware and principal-based Policy to the generated routes first. If an existing contract needs an adapter, extend that module using the public Server manager and retain its authorization checks; missing built-in authentication alone is not a reason to replace the routes. Never trust browser-supplied ownership.

### Preview and content access

Preview supports safe raster images, PDF via a fetched blob, text/Markdown and audio/video. HTML/SVG/XML previews and unsafe URL schemes are rejected. DOCX, XLSX and PPTX use lazily loaded `@silurus/ooxml` viewers to render locally from `FileRecord.contentUrl`; their content is not sent to a third-party preview service. Legacy DOC/XLS/PPT and OpenDocument formats use Office Online, which requires an internet-accessible absolute URL and cannot use the App session.

OOXML, PDF and text fetches use same-origin credentials. An App-owned content route protected by same-origin session cookies can therefore serve restricted previews, provided it checks the caller's record access. Cross-origin fetches omit credentials and require CORS; an external cookie-protected URL is not supported by this default path. The Repository API client's Bearer token is not automatically attached to content fetches.

For Bearer-only content authorization, adapt the installed Registry source in the App. Add an authenticated content loader to the OOXML fetch path and `PreviewBody`'s PDF/text fetches, and adapt download and media/image paths as needed. Resolve authentication through the App's supported client/session services and send credentials only to the trusted content endpoint. Do not put tokens in `contentUrl`. If the adapter creates blob URLs, keep an App-owned trusted URL set, pass it to the relevant `resolveSafeFileUrl` calls, and revoke URLs when replaced or unmounted. Merely assigning a `blob:` URL to `FileRecord.contentUrl` is insufficient: the default components reject untrusted blob URLs.

evidence.excerpt:
## 4. authz: page authorization

`authz` is a `{ resource: { type, id }, action }` request, `'skip'`, or `'unrestricted'`. Nothing is inferred from the route name. Menus, page loading and the permission set page all read the resolved value, which comes from the root down:

- **A page that declares `authz`** uses it. A malformed value raises an error at registration.
- **A nested page that omits it** inherits the value of its nearest ancestor page, through navigation groups and any number of levels. A child that declares its own value overrides it for itself and its descendants.
- **The first page on a path that omits it** still registers, and the application still starts, with a development warning naming the route, its path and the default applied. A protected App page (`auth: 'required'`) or a settings page becomes `'unrestricted'`: only identities with unrestricted access, such as root, may open it, and it is hidden from everyone else's menus. A `guest` or `optional` App page, or a dev page, becomes `'skip'`.

**Always declare `authz` on the first page of every path.** The default keeps an omission from stopping the application; it is not a design choice. `'unrestricted'` may also be declared explicitly for a page only root may open; nothing grants it, so it never appears in the permission set page.

**Rules:**

- The check follows `authz`, regardless of `auth`.
- A navigation group cannot have `authz` (it raises an error at registration) and carries no permission of its own.
- A child page renders only after the parent page's check passes. Writing `'skip'` on a child page does not bypass the parent page's check.
- Without permission, the menu entry is hidden, and opening the URL directly shows "Access denied" without loading the page component. While the check is pending, protected content is not shown; a failed check is treated as no permission.
- Only root, which is unrestricted, holds every page permission. Every other identity, including one you think of as an administrator, needs the page grant in a permission set. When the feature is for people who do not have it yet, seed or assign the grant as the `nocobase-app-plugin-authorization` Skill describes, and say in your report who can open the page.
- **`auth` and `authz` both act only in the browser**. Endpoints must do their own authentication and authorization (`auth.required()`, `authorization.middleware()`) and cannot rely on the page's settings.
- **A page grant opens the page and authorizes no endpoint.** The endpoints of a restricted App page check a business action instead: an action of a `composite` registered with `authz.compositeResources.define`, which the same permission set grants beside the page. Design the composite, its actions and data scopes with the `nocobase-app-plugin-authorization` Skill; never make an endpoint check `page` `access`.
